itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Islamabad, city tour
Day 2: Fly to Skardu (one-hour flight)
Day 3: Free acclimatization day in Skardu
Day 4: Drive Skardu to Hushe (6-7 hrs, 120km)
Day 5: Trek Hushe to Parbisan (3-4 hrs)
Day 6: Trek Parbisan to Brumbrama (3-4 hrs)
Day 7: Trek Brumbrama to Masherbrum Base Camp (3-4 hrs)
Day 8: Free day at base camp
Day 9: Return trek to Brumbrama (4 hrs)
Day 10: Trek to Hushe village
Day 11: Drive Hushe to Skardu (6-7 hrs)
Day 12: Fly Skardu to Islamabad
Day 13: Departure transfer to airport
pros: Fully transparent sliding-scale pricing for both foreign ($1,250-$1,950) and Pakistani (PKR 85,000-445,000) trekkers
Licensed local operator (License No. DTS-GB-046)
All meals and beverages included throughout, plus satellite phone and first-aid kit
Built-in acclimatization day in Skardu (Day 3) before the trek
Government permits and professional licensed guide included
cons: Tight 14kg porter weight limit per person; excess luggage is charged extra
No fixed maximum group size stated ('varies depending on the itinerary')
Hotel meals not explicitly listed as included despite hotel nights
Personal insurance, visa fees and trekking equipment are all on the trekker
verdict: A transparent, licensed local operator with clear dual foreign/local pricing and full meal coverage on trek. The undefined group size and 14kg porter cap are the main caveats.
excludes: International airfare, visa, personal insurance, personal trekking equipment, excess luggage over 14kg, tips and miscellaneous; hotel meals not clearly covered.

pros: Clear fixed price of US$1,800 per adult with a stated US$250 deposit
Local operator with English-speaking guide, assistant guides, cooks and porters
Trek meals, kitchen and toilet tents, staff insurance and safety rope included
Complimentary extras (umbrella, sunscreen, t-shirt, entrance fees)
Alternative overland route offered if the Skardu flight is cancelled
cons: Lowest porter baggage allowance of the set at 12.5kg per person
Main meals at hotels explicitly excluded (only trek meals covered)
Group size not stated on the page
Sleeping bags and personal equipment not provided
verdict: A solid fixed-price local option with strong staff support and thoughtful extras. Watch the 12.5kg porter limit and the fact hotel meals are not included.
excludes: International/domestic airfare, airport taxes, excess baggage over 12.5kg, sleeping bags, personal clothing/equipment, main meals at hotels, drinks, laundry, insurance, medical/helicopter rescue.

pros: Clear small-group cap of 2-12 people
Accommodation, meals, internal flights and airport transfers all bundled per FAQ
Listed on TourRadar with a 5.0/5 rating (10 reviews) and full-refund cancellation policy
Rated 'Low Intensity', suiting less-experienced trekkers
TourRadar holds payment until the tour departs (buyer protection)
cons: Highest price in this set at from US$2,360 per person (booked via marketplace, not direct)
Inclusions only summarized; specific items not itemized on the page
Insurance explicitly not included
Minimum age requirement of 24+ excludes younger trekkers
No porter weight limit stated on the page
verdict: A small-group, marketplace-booked trek with strong reviews and buyer protection, but at a premium price and with thin inclusion detail. Best if you value TourRadar's refund safeguards over direct-operator transparency.
excludes: Insurance; other exclusions not itemized on the page (inclusions only summarized as accommodation, meals, internal flights, airport transfers).

pros: Established local operator running since 1997
Clear fixed price of US$2,480 per person
All trek meals, camping equipment and staff insurance included
English-speaking guide, cook and porters provided
Built-in flexibility with fly-or-drive options if Skardu flights are cancelled
cons: Low 12.5kg porter baggage allowance per person
Only a 2-person minimum stated; no group-size cap given
Hotel extras (drinks, laundry) and sleeping bags excluded
Among the more expensive options at US$2,480
verdict: A long-established local operator with transparent fixed pricing and solid staff support. The 12.5kg porter limit and higher price are the trade-offs.
excludes: International/domestic airfare, excess baggage over 12.5kg, sleeping bags, personal clothing/equipment, hotel extras (drinks, laundry), medical/helicopter rescue, liability insurance.

pros: Most generous porter allowance in the set at 15kg per person
All meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) included, plus satellite phone and first-aid kit
Detailed itinerary with distances and elevations for each trekking day
Licensed Pakistani operator (Government Licence 396, '29 Years of Excellence')
Permits and waste fees included
cons: No pricing listed anywhere on the page
Group size not specified
Single room supplement charged extra
Sleeping bag not provided
verdict: The most detailed itinerary with the best porter allowance (15kg) and full meal coverage, from a long-licensed local operator. The lack of any published price is the one real gap.
excludes: International airfare, visa fees, personal insurance, staff tips, sleeping bag, personal expenses, single room supplement, and anything not in the inclusions list.
